posts: CC Commander v8.1.0: a guided AI PM layer for Claude Code, Cowork Desktop and Codex. Core stays free forever. One plugin, one install. 🧭
Type `/ccc` and pick Build, Review or Ship. No prompt-catalog digging. `/ccc-suggest` reads your repo and recommends the next step.
What ships: 84 skills, 22 specialist agents (architect, reviewer, debugger, designer and more), lifecycle hooks, a HUD mod, six workflows and eight plugin evals.
The PM pattern: a planner stays in control while focused agents build, review and audit. Findings get adversarially verified before they reach you.
It runs where you work: Claude Code Desktop, the CLI, the Codex CLI, and any MCP-capable IDE.
Honest caveat: Codex lacks some Claude hook events, so a few hooks are remapped or dropped. Skills, agents and workflows still work.

Install in Claude Code:
`/plugin install commander --marketplace KevinZai/commander`

Repo, MIT licensed: https://github.com/KevinZai/commander
Feedback welcome. Disclosure: some integrations use affiliate links.

linkedin.text:
I just shipped CC Commander v8.1.0, an open-source PM layer for Claude Code, Cowork Desktop and Codex.

The problem: AI coding agents are powerful but leave you managing prompts instead of projects.

What it does:
- `/ccc` gives a click-first menu: Build, Review, Ship
- 84 skills and 22 specialist agents, with a planner coordinating focused builders and reviewers
- Workflows where every finding is adversarially verified before it reaches you
- Works in Claude Code Desktop, the CLI, Codex and MCP-capable IDEs

Core is free and MIT licensed. One caveat: Codex lacks some Claude hook events, so a few hooks are remapped.

Install: /plugin install commander --marketplace KevinZai/commander
Repo: https://github.com/KevinZai/commander

What would you want a PM layer for agents to do first?
